senior-australian-public-servants-and-ad.core: Posted in last 7 days Senior Australian Public Servants & Advisers - Public Profile Debate Imagine it's Monday morning, and a nasty post about your department's work is gaining traction online. In two different offices, it's a sliding doors moment. In one office, the Secretary has stayed quiet online, wary of saying the wrong thing. In the other, the Secretary has been intentional, so people already know where to go to hear from them. Whose office would you rather be in? That's the question at the heart of my piece in The Mandarin today, built on my recent conversation with Mike Kaiser (Secretary at DCCEEW) on the Your Digital Reputation podcast. Mike calls the public service's "seen and not heard" convention outdated, and believes now is the time to have the debate about whether being seen and not heard is still fit for purpose. I agree. So, who wants to be part of it? If you hold a senior role in the public service or advise those who do, I'd love to hear from you. Please send me a PM or connection request, and I'd be happy to include you in an evidence-based discussion. Thanks Peter Gearin for helping drive this forward. The Mandarin

community-banks-and-credit-unions-first-.core: Posted in last 7 days Community Banks & Credit Unions - First 90 Days Onboarding I'm working on an article for The Financial Brand and seeking expert insight. Here's the abstract: The Custom Welcome: Designing the First 90 Days Around the Individual, Not the Product. Standard onboarding treats every new checking customer the same, even though one is a young professional with a new direct deposit and another is a retiree consolidating accounts. This article looks at how institutions are adapting early communications and activation steps to each new account holder’s behavior, such as whether they’ve set up direct deposit, enrolled in digital banking, or started using their debit card. It covers the milestones that signal a lasting relationship and how automated, timely outreach can respond to them. It extends the onboarding and checking-primacy pieces from the point of account opening to the point of real engagement. If you represent a community bank or credit union with a story to share on this topic, I would love to speak with you next week. Please drop me a note in the comments or DM me. TIA! I’m developing an article for the Association for Women in Science about tattoos, professionalism, and belonging in STEM, and I’m looking for femme-identifying individuals willing to share their experiences. I want to explore a deceptively simple question: Who gets to look like a scientist? I’m especially interested in speaking with tattooed individuals working or studying in science, technology, engineering, mathematics, medicine, or related fields. Have you ever: • Covered a tattoo for an interview, presentation, conference, or client meeting? • Wondered whether visible ink would affect how others perceived your competence or authority? • Received positive or negative comments about your tattoos at work? • Noticed different expectations for tattooed women and men? • Felt more comfortable displaying your tattoos after gaining seniority? • Used your tattoos to express your scientific interests, culture, identity, or personal history? • Found that visible tattoos helped you connect with students, patients, colleagues, or the public? I would also like to hear from femme-identifying persons who have visible tattoos and have never experienced professional consequences. Positive and mixed experiences are important to this story. I can conduct interviews by email or video call. If you are interested, please comment below, send me a direct message, or tag someone whose perspective should be included. Confidentiality or the use of a pseudonym is available. Please share this post with your STEM networks! #womeninstem #femmeinstem #stemcareers #tattoos #workplaceculture #professionalism #sciencecommunication Photo for tax with one of my visible tattoos by Tyler McCall at Golden Pony Tattoo In Aurora, CO. lawyers-and-law-students-ethics-and-well.headline: Lawyers & Law Students - Ethics & Wellbeing PRIME Module Podcast
lawyers-and-law-students-ethics-and-well.author: Professor Lydia Bleasdale
lawyers-and-law-students-ethics-and-well.core: Posted in last 7 days Lawyers & Law Students - Ethics & Wellbeing PRIME Module Podcast I'm giving my final semester one lecture of our PRIME (Professions, Reflections, Identity, Motivations and Ethics) module this week, focusing on how ethics and wellbeing interrelate. We've covered Mary Gentile's Giving Voice to Values framework, which we've then applied when considering the Post Office Horizon Scandal, Enron, and the Hillsborough disaster: who does/doesn't speak up? Why? How can we better prepare our students to be able to speak up when they know what the right thing to do is? We've also asked them to consider what a 'good' lawyer is, and how this fits with things like cause lawyering. Next term, we have a greater focus on the formative and summative assessments, but cover new topics too (imposterism, belonging, accent bias - all within the legal profession, and Law schools). Thanks to Kisby Dickinson Clare Patton (Clar Ui Pheatin) Alex Batesmith for their (as ever) excellent lectures! One of my favourite parts of teaching this module is being able to interview a huge range of people for our module podcasts. These are now a compulsory part of the preparation for each workshop, and this year we're lucky enough to have even more to draw upon in our discussions (and for the students to draw upon in their reflective assessments). The focus of each interview differs, but we always try to link them to at least one of our topics, bringing that topic to life in a different way / providing a different perspective on it. Thanks to some SLSA funding, I've been interviewing students who took PRIME last year and have consistently heard how much they loved the podcasts - so, thank you to all our guests who so generously gave us their time this year or last. If anyone would like to be interviewed this year or for the module in future, please drop me a line and you can join this illustrious list: Patrick McCann Lolan E. Sagoe-Moses Carla Hoppe Mandy Rees Simon Price Niamh Warnock Lucinda Soon Professor Alex Nicholson Richard Moorhead Dalton Harrison Nysha Chantel G. elkan abrahamson Sean Jones KC Neil Atkinson Richard Harper

hospitality-pros-and-guests-worldwide-be.author: Elizabeth Oke, AITPN
hospitality-pros-and-guests-worldwide-be.core: Posted in last 7 days Hospitality Pros & Guests Worldwide - Behind Closed Doors Hospitality has no borders. Neither should the stories behind it. Every country has a hospitality industry. Every hospitality professional has an experience. And every guest has a story to tell. Some stories inspire us. Some challenge the way we think. Others reveal realities that deserve more attention. This is why I created BEHIND CLOSED DOORS, an initiative under LIZZY TALKS HOSPITALITY. Are you a hotelier, receptionist, housekeeper, chef, restaurant worker, hospitality manager, short-term rental operator or guest? Have you experienced something in hospitality that deserves to be shared? I want to hear from YOU, wherever you are in the world. Perhaps it's an unforgettable experience, a workplace challenge, a lesson learned, an operational issue or something that made you see hospitality differently. I want to hear your story. This is an open invitation to hospitality professionals and guests across the globe. Your location, position or years of experience do not matter. Your voice does. You can share your experience through the form below. You also have the option to indicate whether you consent to your story being shared publicly. Let's bring different perspectives together, encourage meaningful conversations and learn from experiences across borders. One industry. Different experiences. Countless stories. Let's talk hospitality! 🌍 Share your story here: https://lnkd.in/es4mrXn2 #LizzyTalksHospitality #BehindClosedDoors #GlobalHospitality #HospitalityStories #HospitalityProfessionals

delhi-parents-navigating-nursery-admissi.author: Lakshima Sareen
delhi-parents-navigating-nursery-admissi.core: Posted in last 7 days Delhi Parents Navigating Nursery Admissions - Costs & Pressure Media Request | How much does it take to get a three-year-old into a good school in Delhi? 🏫 With nursery admissions for the 2027–28 academic session approaching, parents are preparing for another year of intense competition for limited seats in reputed schools. From admission-related expenses and alleged demands for expensive gifts or donations to families considering a move to Noida or Gurugram for better schooling options, the race for a good school is influencing major family decisions. But how does this pressure affect parents and young children? How much are families willing to spend or compromise for a school seat? And is this competition justified at such an early age? I am looking to speak to parents who have experienced or are preparing for Delhi nursery admissions. If you are willing to share your experience for a feature story, please comment below or drop me a direct message. #DelhiNurseryAdmissions #DelhiSchools #Parenting #Education #MediaRequest #JournoRequest
